tip: The Italian present covers both English tenses: compro il pane = I buy and I am buying bread.
Regular -are verbs take -i for tu: cucinare becomes tu cucini = you cook.
Every noi form ends in -iamo, whatever the verb group: noi prepariamo = we prepare.
Some -ire verbs insert -isc- in the singular: preferire gives lei preferisce. Same pattern as finire and capire.
gli is the masculine plural the before a vowel or s plus consonant: gli occhiali = the glasses. Otherwise it is i.
To say yes or no, Italian adds di: dice di no = she says no, direi di si = I would say yes.
bere is irregular with a hidden v: bevo, bevi, lui beve = he drinks. The stem is bev-.
gg before i sounds like the English j: leggi = you read, said LEDJ-ee. Before a or o it hardens.
da marks from or a starting point: lavoro da casa = I work from home.
pagare takes a direct object with no for: pago il conto = I pay the bill, pago il caffe = I pay for the coffee.
Drop the article before a singular family member with a possessive: tua madre = your mother, not la tua madre.
rispondere needs a before its object: risponde al telefono = he answers the phone. al = a plus il.
portare covers bring, carry, and wear at once: porto un regalo = I bring a gift, porto gli occhiali = I wear glasses.
macchina literally means machine, but in everyday speech it means car: guidi la macchina = you drive the car.
sperare joins a following verb with di: spera di vincere = he hopes to win.
Descriptive adjectives usually follow the noun: vestiti nuovi = new clothes, literally clothes new.
Verbs ending -gare add an h before i to keep the hard g: navigare gives navighi = you browse.
Verbs in -giare keep a single i for tu: assaggiare becomes assaggi = you taste, never assaggii.
provare links to a following verb with a, not di: prova a capire = she tries to understand.
controllare usually means to check, not to control: controlli il calendario = you check the calendar.
Use lo, not il, before s plus consonant, z, or gn: lo spettacolo = the show, lo zaino = the backpack.
Masculine un takes no apostrophe before a vowel: un albero = a tree. The feminine does: un'amica.
acqua naturale means still water, not natural: beviamo acqua naturale. Sparkling is acqua frizzante.
Meals use fare, not avere: fa colazione = he has breakfast, with no article before colazione.
volere is irregular: voglio, vuoi, vuole, vogliamo, volete, vogliono. lui vuole = he wants.
Age uses avere, not to be: ho ventitre anni = I am twenty-three, literally I have twenty-three years.
Weather uses fare: fa caldo = it is hot, fa freddo = it is cold, literally it makes heat.
tenere is irregular: tengo, tieni, lui tiene = he holds. The stressed e becomes ie.
Being right uses avere: hai ragione = you are right, literally you have reason. The opposite is avere torto.
The adjective matches the noun's gender: la neve e bianca (f), but il muro e bianco (m).
Months take a: a settembre = in September, a giugno = in June.
camera means a room or bedroom, not a photo camera (that is macchina fotografica): la mia camera = my room.
soldi (money) is always plural in Italian: risparmio soldi = I save money, non ho soldi = I have no money.
il fine settimana (weekend) is masculine and never changes in the plural: i fine settimana.
seguire un corso means to take a course, not to follow it: segue un corso online = she takes an online course.
Italian is under the shower, not in it: canti sotto la doccia = you sing in the shower. sotto = under.
In Italy a bar is a cafe serving coffee and pastries: ci incontriamo al bar = we meet at the cafe.
Languages take the definite article: imparare il francese = to learn French, parlo l'italiano.
uscire is irregular: esco, esci, esce = I, you, he go out. The u of uscire turns into e in these forms.
sperare che triggers the subjunctive: spero che il tempo migliori = I hope the weather improves, migliori not migliora.
bisogna is impersonal, always third person, meaning one must: bisogna che partiamo presto = we must leave early.
ci vediamo literally means we see each other and is the normal see you: ci vediamo domani = see you tomorrow.
c'e means there is: c'e un supermercato? = is there a supermarket? The plural is ci sono, there are.
ne stands in for of it or of them: ne ha di piu grandi? = do you have any bigger ones (of them)?
portare a spasso is the set phrase for taking out for a walk: porti a spasso il cane = you walk the dog.
dare da mangiare is the fixed phrase for to feed: da da mangiare al pesce = he feeds the fish.
scegliere is irregular: io scelgo but tu scegli = I, you choose. The gl and lg swap in the io form.
could have uses the past conditional: avrebbero potuto aiutare = they could have helped.
The voi ending for -ere verbs is -ete: voi leggete = you all read.
desiderare attaches straight to an infinitive, no linking word: desidera cambiare citta = he wishes to change cities.
andare is irregular: vado, vai, va, andiamo, andate, vanno = go. io vado = I go.
da before a person means at or to their place: va dal dottore = she goes to the doctor's. dal = da plus il.
fare la spesa is the set phrase for grocery shopping: faccio la spesa. The plural fare le spese means clothes shopping.
Adjectives ending in -e use -i for the plural in both genders: felici = happy, from felice.
potrei is the polite could I: potrei avere il menu? = could I have the menu, softer than posso.
Add -mente to an adjective to make an adverb, like English -ly: lento becomes lentamente = slowly.
sapere plus an infinitive means to know how to: sa cucinare = he can cook. potere would mean is allowed to.
Telling time is plural: che ore sono? = what time is it, answered sono le tre. Only one o'clock is singular: e l'una.
